title: T1071.004 — Application Layer Protocol - DNS
subtitle: Eight steps of a DNS tunnel, from a quiet implant to containment.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: A dormant implant wakes up
steps.caption: A beacon on FIN-SRV-02 (10.20.8.22) wakes after 13 idle days. It needs a channel that always works, and every network allows DNS. The server makes about two normal lookups per minute, so a quiet channel hides well. build a per-host baseline of lookup volume before you can spot a change
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Encode and ask
steps.caption: The implant encodes host information with base32 (a way to write any data using 32 letters and digits) into a subdomain: mfuhq3ttq2f7w2ndogq7c3u62bvdvibqbfgs5iynha3deq.sync-log[.]net . It asks the internal resolver for a TXT record. a 46-character random-looking label is not a person typing. Alert on label length
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The answer carries orders
steps.caption: The attacker's authoritative server (ns1.sync-log[.]net, 203.0.113.77) answers with a TXT record that holds a base32 task. The resolver caches the answer and returns it, and the implant decodes the orders. servers rarely need TXT answers. TXT from a host that never used TXT is a strong signal
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The 30-second loop
steps.caption: The implant checks in every 30 seconds, always TXT, always the same zone. Over one hour that is 120 small queries, each under 150 bytes. per-host periodicity beats per-domain detection. Bin lookups per host per minute
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Files out through names
steps.caption: To steal a 100 KB document, the implant splits it into base32 pieces and sends about 4,000 queries over 40 minutes. No port opens, no large upload happens. The file leaves in name-sized pieces. watch volume, label length, and entropy per host. 4,000 TXT in 40 minutes is theft, not lookups
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: The resolver sees the spike
steps.caption: DNS analytics compare FIN-SRV-02 with its own 30-day baseline: TXT volume is 210 times normal and label entropy is far above normal. The DNS-VOL-01 rule fires. alert on deviation from each host's own baseline, not on one global average
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Confirm the tunnel
steps.caption: The analyst replays the queries: a fixed 30-second cadence, one single zone, encoded answers. A short capture from the host shows the same labels. A sinkhole test proves C2: the resolver answers bad names with a fake address, and the implant keeps retrying it anyway. confirm with two independent views, resolver log plus host capture, before you isolate
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Sinkhole and close
steps.caption: The team sinkholes sync-log[.]net on the internal resolver to 127.0.0.1, isolates FIN-SRV-02, and pins all egress DNS to internal resolvers only. DoH and DoT to the internet are blocked so the implant cannot rebuild the channel. sinkholing buys time. Fix the egress policy so the next implant finds a closed door
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.
